QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_15

question.text: Unlike operating expenses, Transaction Expenses (brokerage, STT, depository charges, exchange costs) for an AIF are:

answer.text: Paid only from the incentive fee pool
Absorbed entirely by the Investment Manager
Borne on actuals without any limit

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.1: AIF bears and pays all transaction expenses on actual basis WITHOUT any limit, allocated pro-rata by Capital Contributions or NAV. Includes brokerage, depository, custodian transaction, STT, exchange charges. The Trap: Option A confuses with operating expense cap. Option C is commercially unreasonable. Option B mixes fee pools. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests transaction expenses for Cat III; VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers STT mechanics in detail. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a high-turnover Cat III long-short fund, transaction costs can easily exceed 1% p.a. — disclose an illustrative churn rate in the PPM so LPs understand the 'invisible' drag. Broker panel selection also matters: LPs often ask for best-execution policy documentation.
